intro: A stroke is a time-critical emergency, so recognising it fast with FAST and calling 999 at once can save a life.
points: Call 999 at once the moment you suspect a stroke, because time is brain and treatments only work if given quickly.
Use FAST: check Face, Arms and Speech, act on any single sign, and remember T stands for Time to call 999.
Still call 999 even if the signs pass, as it may be a TIA warning that a larger stroke could follow.
Give the person nothing to eat, drink or swallow, because a stroke can make swallowing unsafe and cause choking.
Note the time the symptoms started, or when the person was last seen well, and pass it to the paramedics.
Stay with the person, keep them calm and comfortable, and never drive them to hospital yourself.
